Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to kick off the Dedicated capacity onboarding as soon as possible. Before the initial implementation sprint we need to lock down a few design decisions so our infra team can provision networking and estimate cross-region egress. Quick questions below — could you confirm by EOD or point to the best owner?

1) Region: our traffic is primarily west coast (70% US-West) but we expect a multi-region failover. Is it reasonable to start with a single us-west pool + warm standby in us-east, or should we recommend active-active from day one?

2) Burst policy: we have spiky nightly batch jobs (2–4x baseline for ~45 minutes). What gating do you need in the capacity matrix to map to burst credits vs reserved capacity?

3) Autoscaling: desired SLO is p95 latency <120ms for short text generation (avg seq 60 tokens). What concurrency/worker configuration do you recommend for Llama-2-13B quantized?

4) Timeline & procurement: we have procurement windows for May 28 sign-off and need a draft SOW to attach.

I've attached our initial capacity spreadsheet — filled a couple of rows. Happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

Best,
Tara

Hi Tara —

Great to see Orchid moving fast. Short answers up front, then a proposed next step and asks below.

1) Region: start with single-region (us-west) + warm standby in us-east is the pragmatic path for your traffic profile. We recommend active-passive for M0–M1 phase to reduce cost and operational blast radius; we can automate failover and health checks for the standby. Active-active is reasonable at scale but requires cross-region KV cache warming considerations.

2) Burst policy: please complete the "burst window" and "expected peak multiplier" columns in the attached capacity matrix. From what you described, the model of reserved baseline + burst credits for 2–4x 45-minute windows fits well. We'll map burst windows to short-term capacity reservations (warm nodes) vs transient GPU borrowing.

3) Autoscaling & concurrency: for Llama-2-13B quantized on A100-class hosts we typically recommend targeting 8–12 concurrent streams per GPU for short sequences, with a continuous-batching target of 50–100ms batching latency. For p95 <120ms we will tune worker count + batch cutoff; we'll include a recommended profile in the activation runbook.

4) Timeline & SOW: attached draft SOW_Orchid_v1.pdf and a short policy note redwood-burst-policy-options.md. We can produce a procurement-ready SOW by May 25 if you confirm baseline committed tokens and burst windows.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync tomorrow (Wed, May 20) to review the matrix live and lock region + burst policy. Can you confirm availability (9–11am PT or 2–4pm PT)?

CC'd Marissa (CS lead) and Sean (ops) to own activation tasks once we lock decisions.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
